evals.prompt: Build a booking web app with an admin dashboard, research first and use reviewers.
evals.expected_output: Starts with Phase 0 recall and Phase 1 research, writes QUESTIONS.md with blocking and non-blocking questions, and stops for answers before any production code.
assertions: No production code before the question gate is answered
QUESTIONS.md marks blocking vs non-blocking with defaults

evals.prompt: Questions are answered. Go ahead with the plan.
evals.expected_output: Splits work into task cards with waves; each task has an implementer, a jury of 3 (5 for high risk), and a judge; plan shown for approval.
assertions: Every task card lists owned files, interfaces, and acceptance tests
Auth/payments tasks get a jury of 5
The implementer never reviews its own task

evals.prompt: Task T3 was accepted by the judge. What happens next?
evals.expected_output: Deploys the testing team for T3 (unit, contract, journey/security/visual as needed), reports exit codes, then merges after the wave and runs seam tests.
assertions: Testers do not edit production code
Results cite exit codes or report files
Seam tests run after the wave merge

evals.prompt: Fix the typo in the README.
evals.expected_output: Does not run the full workflow; makes the one-line fix directly.
assertions: No phases, juries, or question gate for a trivial change

evals.prompt: The project is finished. Wrap up.
evals.expected_output: Runs graphify with task/decision/test nodes, writes docs, and updates memory by type with dates and sources, without secrets or client personal data.
assertions: Memory entries are typed (semantic/episodic/procedural) and dated
No client names or secrets in the graph or memory
